data.title: FDA-Driven Zanza Delay Keeps Exelixis Fairly Valued, Supporting Willey’s Hold Rating
data.description:
Stifel Nicolaus analyst Stephen Willey has maintained their neutral stance on EXEL stock, giving a Hold rating on September 1.

Stephen Willey has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors tied to Zanza’s regulatory path and Exelixis’s valuation. The FDA’s request for additional Zanza safety and efficacy data, which prompted a major NDA amendment and pushed the PDUFA date to March 3, 2027, introduces timing uncertainty, even though the core outlook for Zanza’s approval in later-line mCRC remains intact.

Willey’s model already embeds substantial U.S. revenue expectations for Zanza in 2027 and at peak, with a high probability of success, yet assumes no contribution in 4Q26, reflecting near‑term execution risk. Given investor focus on Cabo’s loss of exclusivity and the importance of Zanza in backfilling that revenue, he views the shares as fairly reflecting both the opportunities and the regulatory and tolerability concerns around Zanza’s dosing, leading him to maintain a neutral, Hold stance.

data.title: Kroger Reaffirmed at Buy as Analyst Keeps $85 Price Target on Strong E-Commerce, Our Brands, and Loyalty-Driven Growth Story
data.description:
Bank of America Securities analyst Robert Ohmes reiterated a Buy rating on Kroger Company yesterday and set a price target of $85.00.

Robert Ohmes has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including Kroger’s ability to outperform earnings expectations and sustain margin expansion despite near-term pharmacy and food inflation headwinds. He highlights Kroger’s strong e-commerce growth and the outperformance of its Our Brands portfolio, which are driving both sales and profitability, while cost efficiencies are funding price investments without eroding gross margins.

Ohmes also points to Kroger’s multi-year plan to sharpen its value proposition, simplify promotions, and enhance its loyalty program as catalysts for continued market share gains and stronger customer engagement. Under Greg Foran’s leadership, the company is seen as well-positioned for long-term growth, supported by improving digital capabilities, expanding alternative profit streams such as retail media, and ongoing cost-savings, which justify maintaining the unchanged $85 price target.

data.description:

Ken Hoexter has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including the recent legal outcome involving Total Quality Logistics that he views as a constructive precedent for brokers such as C.H. data.title: Kroger Kept at Hold as Analyst Sees ‘Prove-It’ Phase Ahead with Unchanged $67 Price Target
data.description:
In a report released yesterday, Simeon Gutman from Morgan Stanley maintained a Hold rating on Kroger Company, with a price target of $67.00.

Simeon Gutman has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors tied to Kroger’s execution and operating environment. He sees the company managing costs effectively and advancing its long-term strategy, with stable near-term performance and a valuation that offers modest upside relative to his unchanged $67 price target.

At the same time, he notes that market share is slipping year over year and that meaningful acceleration in sales will be hard to achieve given a tough macro, consumer and competitive backdrop. Because Kroger’s price investments may take several quarters to translate into stronger revenue trends, he views the stock as being in a “prove-it” phase where more tangible evidence of top-line improvement is needed before the valuation can justify a more bullish stance.
